1	# Playthrough Strategy
2	
3	Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
4	its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
5	area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.
6	
7	## General Strategy
8	
9	- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
10	
11	## Recruiting Units
12	
13	In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.
14	
15	The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.
16	
17	## Promoting Units
18	
19	Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.
20	
21	In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.
22	
23	## Broad strategy notes
24	
25	Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.
26	
27	- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
28	- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
29	- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
30	- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
31	- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
32	- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
33	- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.

518	**Agent notes:**
519	
520	- Won on turn 50 by s01 on attempt 1, picking up a game already on turn 24 (Hector was 15/40). No deaths. Farina not recruited: only about 9,000G available, never spoke to her.
521	- Any unit can score, not just the lord: Canas (NE), Dart (N), Dart (SW). Points persist after the unit leaves. Seize never appears. Clearing all enemies does not win, and Door Keys, ruins and shops do nothing for points.
522	- Hector stood on the SW gate on t24 and I backed out without Waiting. Waiting there would have scored at once and saved a long detour. On a retry: Wait on the nearest gate first.
523	- Enemies seen: cavaliers, steel-bow archers, and a Bishop with Purge (range 3-10). Monks arrived in pairs near the NE castle from about t38; none appeared after Canas held that gate from t43, though I can't prove the cause.
524	- Lake is impassable even for Dart, and the eastern mountains block walkers. The route to the north runs over the middle bridge, along the shore, then over the wide bridge. Ballistae hit across the lake (5 uses each, Wil used one up); several unused ones remain.
525	- Vendor (Mend, Thunder, Lightning, Flux) and Armory (steel weapons) are just north of the eastern mountains. Bought one Steel axe for Hawkeye (360G), but did not check his inventory afterwards. Funds at handover about 8,697G.
526	- Army at handover: Hector Lv18 (42 HP, brave/hand/steel axes, hammer), Hawkeye Lv6 (Killer axe, low on uses), Wil gained a level (31 max HP) and has only the bow I saw him fire; I never opened his inventory. Canas (Nosferatu, Heal, 2 Door Keys) had a level-up screen, level unconfirmed. Dart Lv8 (steel axe, hand axe, torch). Only these five plus Merlinus are on the Unit list, which is a very thin army.
527	- Canas is fragile against Purge and took several hits unnoticed: read every HP after each enemy phase. Nosferatu on Monks heals him safely.
528	- Ending: saved to the highlighted Ch. 25 slot (the save prompt's default), which is the one assumed to be in use. Chapter 26 title card was missed; Preparations shows "Chapter 26", objective Survive.

544	- Objective as shown: Survive, 11 turns (HUD "1/11 Turn").
545	- s02 attempt 1 lost on the first enemy phase: Lyn died beside Hector on open plain and the game went straight to GAME OVER. Lyn's death ends the chapter. I had not read her HP before placing her.
546	- Start: north group Hector, Lyn, Eliwood, Louise, Pent; south group Wil, Dart, Canas, Hawkeye, Matthew, Ninian, Merlinus's tent. Louise and Pent are controllable but L skips them; select them with the cursor.

551	
552	- Died: Dart (t3 enemy phase, left on the flank and hit by two wyverns) and Wil (t11 enemy phase, left on the ballista beside two wyverns after his last shot). Pulling both back would probably have saved them. Vaida was never attacked on my phase and spoke in Ch. 27's opening, so she is alive for Ch. 29.
553	- Lords stayed east on t1, which solved the opening. Lyn was at 7/23 from t4 after I attacked with her for 2 damage a hit, so Hector carried her from t5 to the end. Eliwood sat boxed in beside Hector, dropped to 8/21 on two separate enemy phases, and Pent healed him both times.

555	- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.
556	- Level-ups seen: Wil Sniper Lv6 (now dead), Hawkeye Berserker Lv8 (Str 21, Spd 12, Def 14). Hawkeye's Killer axe is down from 12 uses; Steel axe was bought last chapter.
557	- Army at handover: Hector Lv18, Hawkeye Lv8, Pent Sage Lv6, Louise Sniper Lv4, Canas Druid Lv8, Lyn Lv13, Eliwood Lv4, Matthew Lv4 (no weapon). No healer besides Pent and Canas. I did not re-read the Unit list after the win.
558	- Merlinus was last seen alive at 18 HP or less with wyverns adjacent on t11; his survival is unconfirmed.
559	- Next time: on the last turns pull ranged units off ballistae when they run out or get surrounded, and never leave a low-HP unit on an open flank. Before attacking with Lyn or Eliwood, read their damage: both do very little to wyverns.
560	- Ending: saved over the highlighted Ch. 26 slot (the one in use); no other choice appeared.

591	### Chapter 28 — Battle before Dawn
592	
593	**Objectives:**
594	
595	Guard Zephiel (Preparations text); "Protect Zephiel for 15 turns" (Status screen); HUD counts "1/15 Turn". Fog map.
596	
597	**Recruits:**

603	
604	**Agent notes:**
605	
606	s04 attempt 1 (lost, GAME OVER on t6 enemy phase): Zephiel was killed while my army was still in the north. Three enemies stood next to him at the start of t6.
607	
608	- Layout: party starts in the walled north yard. East stairs lead to a corridor, whose south wall has a locked door (Door key on Canas; Hawkeye also received one at the end of t1). South of it is the north hall. From there, stairs on the east side lead round to Nino's corridor (Hector reached her tile range by t7) and the far south hall. Zephiel's room opens only on its south side, from the south hall. Walking there takes about 10 turns; enemies arrive by t5.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.

- Army at handover: Hector Lv3+ (17/49 when the map ended, Hammer about 9, Brave axe 3, Heaven seal, no Elixirs left), Hawkeye (at least 60 max HP, Silver axe 2, Steel axe 9, Tomahawk 15, Wolf beil, Chest key), Pent (Elfire 3 at t9, then at most 2 attacks' worth of uses spent, so 0-2 left and unconfirmed; no staff). Eliwood, Lyn, Louise (Silver bow 8), Nils and Vaida (Spear 3) sat out and hold what they held. About 9,900G unspent. No healer on the roster.

content.thinking: I checked the roster and convoy and found no tomes or staves, so Pent can't attack and nobody can heal. Next I'll move Nils's Elixir and the Wolf Beil to Hector and test whether Lyn can use a Heaven Seal.

content.text: Now Lyn: open her menu to pull a Heaven Seal.
Confirming the swap, then backing out to Lyn's menu to try Use.
Use is lit now. Opening it to see whether the seal works on Lyn.
ACTION t0 Lyn: spend Eliwood's Heaven Seal to promote her. At Lv13 with 23 HP and 5 Str she's a liability as a Lord, and a Blade Lord survives far better.
The hand defaults to No, so I'm moving it to Yes and confirming.
The promotion animation is playing, so I'll let it finish.
Lyn is now a Blade Lord. Going back to Preparations to read the map before the fight starts.
Surveying the map, starting south from the throne hall.
Survey's good enough: armored knots to the south and east with chests in walled rooms. Back out and start the fight.
ACTION t1 Merlinus: Yes. Deploying the tent gives field access to the convoy, and the army is short on everything.

content.thinking: I'm holding the throne with Hector, backed by Hawkeye and a wall of units, while Louise covers from range and Pent stays safely behind the line. The green soldiers hold the front stairs for now, and the armor is still far off.

content.text: ACTION t1 Hector: Wait on the throne. It gives Def+2 and Avoid+20, and anyone seizing has to go through him first.
ACTION t1 Vaida: pull into the far corner of the side room, out of reach of the mages over the north wall. With only 3 Spear uses left, she shouldn't be trading blows.

content.thinking: Vaida is backing out of the corner, since archers across the east wall could hit it and wyverns take heavy bow damage. She's moving to a mid-room tile in the south row, two tiles further from them.

content.text: ACTION t1 Louise: hold in the room's middle, out of reach of bows and magic over the walls, and two tiles from the only stair she'd need to shoot at.
Now Wait for Louise, then cycle back to the hall group.
ACTION t1 Lyn: step onto the tile south of the throne, sealing that side of Hector while the guards still hold the stairs.
ACTION t1 Eliwood: take the Support with Hector here, west of the throne. It costs nothing since he was only going to Wait, and the bonus is permanent.
ACTION t1 Pent: move beside Eliwood. He's out of tomes but has the Aid to rescue a lord once the line breaks, so that's his job this chapter.
ACTION t1 Pent: Rescue Eliwood now. The lord with 21 HP can't be targeted while carried, and next turn Pent takes the throne's west tile himself.

content.thinking: Hector is on the throne with Lyn, Hawkeye, and Pent placed around him, and Louise and Vaida are in the east annex. I expect the armor to head toward the green-stairs guards without contact yet.

content.text: Turn 1's enemy phase is still running. The morphs are cutting through the green guards at the stairs faster than I expected, so I'm waiting for it to end and then tightening up around the throne.

content.thinking: With the stair guards falling, the shell moves up now: Hector holds the throne and picks up Lyn, Pent carries Eliwood to close the west tile, and Hawkeye takes the south front line.

content.text: ACTION t2 Hector: rescue Lyn from the throne. He gives up doubling for the turn; in exchange Lyn's 26 HP can't be targeted.
ACTION t2 Pent: Wait on the throne's west tile, carrying Eliwood. He has 42 HP and works as a wall even without a tome.
ACTION t2 Hawkeye: Wait on the south tile as the front line. At 60 HP he should counter hard with his Silver axe equipped.

content.thinking: The shell is closed with the east tile left open on purpose, so only one melee attacker can reach Hector. I'm expecting the mages on the stairs to arrive next phase.

content.text: Still waiting out turn 2's enemy phase. Enemies are converging on the stairs and on the annex's south entrance, and nobody on my side has been hit that I've seen.

content.thinking: The stairs have collapsed and three armored foes plus casters are advancing, so I'm holding the shell: Hawkeye's counters will handle the kills and the throne will heal Hector. Moving out would only open the formation, so everyone stays put.

content.text: Enemies have reached the annex and are on Louise and Vaida. Watching how that goes.

content.thinking: It's turn 4: the hall is intact with Hector at full health, but enemies are next to Louise and Vaida in the annex. I'm checking Vaida's HP before choosing between fighting and retreating.

Louise will shoot the Archer from two tiles, since it's the biggest threat to the wyvern, while Vaida (32/43) pulls back from the casters and bow and keeps 3 Spear uses for counters. The annex can't be escaped because enemies hold both exits, so the throne shell holds.

content.text: Merlinus is at 6/29 with armor beside him and nobody spare to save him. Now Louise's shot.
Forecast on the Poison-axe Morph: 16 HP, 11 ×2 at 100 hit, no counter. That's a guaranteed kill. Comparing it with the Archer before committing.
ACTION t4 Louise: shoot the Longbow Morph. It's 27 HP against about 20+ ×2 at 100 hit, so it dies, removing the one enemy that can snipe Vaida from across the room. Its counter is only 3 at 25 hit.
Louise's kill landed. Now Vaida moves beside her, so the Spear can reach the Poison-axe Morph at two tiles.
ACTION t4 Vaida: Wait beside Louise, blocking her east side. There's no Attack or Item in her menu, which tells me the Spear broke on enemy-phase counters, so she's now a 32 HP wall with no weapon.
ACTION t4 End: Louise killed the Longbow and Vaida shields her. The throne trio holds on purpose. I expect Merlinus to fall or leave, and the annex pair to take the heaviest hits.

content.thinking: The enemy phase is still underway, with a large group massing just east of the throne within Hawkeye's range and green Ostia reinforcements with a healer arriving to the southwest. I'm waiting for my turn.

content.text: ACTION t5 Louise: kill the Luna caster. It has 22 HP and takes 24 at 100 hit, dead on the first arrow, and Luna ignores defense, so it's the biggest threat in this room.

content.thinking: Louise has killed Luna, so Vaida stays put as her east wall while Hector, Pent and Hawkeye hold the shell. I expect the eastern pack to reach the throne this phase.

content.text: Merlinus is pulling out, as expected. Advancing his line.
First contact at the throne: Hawkeye is at 60/60 and countering a 27 HP Morph.
Turn 5's enemy phase is nearly over, with new enemies still coming in from the south. Hawkeye was at 60/60 at last read and Louise at 33/34. I'll check everyone's HP when my phase starts.

content.thinking: They've arrived. Hector and Hawkeye can only strike adjacent units without leaving their tiles, so I'll hit the archer east of the throne first with Hector, then Hawkeye on the armor or morph beside him.

Wolf Beil on the Poison-bow Morph would take 23 of its 83 HP per hit against Hector's 27, with no counter at this range. I'll use the steady 30-use axe rather than burning Brave uses, and Hawkeye's Tomahawk can finish from his tile.

content.text: Poison-bow Morph is down to 4. Hawkeye's Tomahawk hits 32 ×2 at 100, enough to kill almost anything here, so I'm checking the other targets before using it on a 4 HP unit.
ACTION t6 Hawkeye: Tomahawk the Silver-bow Morph, 29 HP against 33 at 100 hit. One throw kills the hardest-hitting bow in range, and the wounded poison archer can wait.
Silver-bow Morph dead. Now reading Pent and the annex.
ACTION t6 Louise: kill the wounded Poison-lance Morph, 12 HP against 14 at 100 hit. It takes one arrow and strips an attacker off Vaida.
Louise leveled up. Letting the card play out.
Vaida is poisoned and about half-dead. With no weapon she can't help Louise beyond blocking a tile, and staying gets her killed. The corridor south is clear now, so I'm checking how far she can flee.
ACTION t6 Vaida: fly down the east corridor, behind the long wall. Four more morphs are massing on the far side of it and can't reach this tile quickly, and she's useless as a wall without a weapon.
ACTION t6 End: three kills this turn and Hector is still at 49/49. Vaida has fled south, and Louise stands alone in the annex at 33 HP. I expect her to be swarmed; Pent holds the west tile.
Still in turn 6's enemy phase, and a new wave of thieves or assassins just came in from the southwest. Both Vaida and Louise have enemies on them. Waiting for turn 7.

content.thinking: The shell is intact and Hector is at full health with four turns left. Next, Hector finishes the wounded archer beside him, then Hawkeye reads his forecasts and strikes the nearby enemy that threatens him most.

content.text: ACTION t7 Hector: Wolf Beil on the 4 HP Poison-bow Morph, 83 hit, no counter at this range. That should be the kill and the XP.
Kill confirmed and Hector leveled up. Waiting for the card.
Now Hawkeye's options, one tile below.

content.thinking: I'm going to throw Tomahawk at the Nosferatu Morph to the south: it has 30 HP against his 37 at 100 hit, so one throw should kill it. It's the only attack dealing real damage here, while Flux and the Poison axe barely scratch.

content.text: Nosferatu is dead. Reading Pent, Louise and Vaida.
Louise is at 33/34 with three melee enemies adjacent and her bow can't hit at one tile. A step east puts them at two tiles, so she can shoot.
ACTION t7 Louise: after the step east, shoot the Poison-lance Morph from two tiles with no counter. Earlier the same target type took 14 per hit, so ×2 should just clear its 26 HP.
Another kill for Louise. Now Vaida.

content.thinking: Vaida will fly back north up the corridor into the annex's far east side, away from the pack to her south. Staying alive longer keeps the enemy chasing her instead of going for the throne.

content.text: The cursor landed on the wall, so no menu opened. One tile left is the room's east column.
ACTION t7 End: three more kills and the shell is unbroken. Vaida keeps running, and Pent stays idle on the west tile on purpose. Four more enemy phases to get through.
Vaida is at 24 and taking fire over the wall from a sword or bow Morph. Waiting on the rest of the phase.

content.thinking: Hector is holding at 50/50 with Hawkeye and Pent still in place, so this turn I'll have Hector take out the caster by the throne and Hawkeye hit the worst adjacent threat, checking Hawkeye's HP first.

content.text: ACTION t8 Hector: Wolf Beil on the Flux Morph, 22 HP against 28 at 85 hit. That's a one-hit kill, and its counter does 0 anyway.
Hector levels again. Waiting for the card, then Hawkeye.
ACTION t8 Hawkeye: Tomahawk the adjacent Poison-bow Morph, 28 HP against 30+ at 100 hit with no counter. Poison ticks are the one thing this shell can't out-heal.
Clean kill. Now the annex: Pent, Louise, Vaida in cycle order.
Louise is still at 33/34. Pent is poisoned but holding. An archer is diagonal to Louise at exactly two tiles, so that's her shot.

content.thinking: My blind presses nearly discarded the White gem, since Louise's broken Silver bow removed Attack from her menu. I've backed out one press at a time, and nothing was lost; she also picked up a Swordslayer.

content.text: ACTION t8 Louise: with no bow, she runs to the annex's NE corner above Vaida. Walls and Vaida leave only one open melee tile against her, which is the best she can get for three more turns.
ACTION t8 End: two kills at the throne. Louise is in the corner with no bow, and Vaida, left idle on purpose, shields her from the south. Three enemy phases remain after this one.
Turn 8's enemy phase is still running. I can't see Louise or Vaida in the annex corner in this frame, only greyed enemies, so they may have fallen. I'll confirm on the Unit list when my phase starts.
Turn 9 and Hector is at 51/51. First I'm opening the Unit list to get the truth on Louise and Vaida.

content.thinking: Everyone is still alive, so my worry was unfounded; Vaida at 18/44 is the only one in real danger, losing 4 HP a turn to poison. Next turn follows the same routine, with Hector and Hawkeye clearing adjacent enemies while Louise and Vaida hold the corner without spending a heal.

content.text: ACTION t9 Hector: Wolf Beil on another Flux Morph, 23 HP against 29 at 88 hit. A one-hit kill, and its counter does 0.
Flux Morph gone. Hawkeye next: opening his Attack option and checking the forecast.

content.thinking: Tomahawk dropped from 11 to 6 uses in one round, since counters at both ranges and his doubling burned through them. I'm moving him to the Steel axe, which counters only at one tile, so the last 6 Tomahawk throws stay in reserve.

content.text: ACTION t9 Hawkeye: Steel axe on the Poison-bow Morph beside him, 28 HP against 30+ at 100 hit, with no counter at one tile. One swing kills and Steel is now his counter weapon.
Killed. Hawkeye is poisoned too, but at 46 HP that's fine for two more turns. Checking the annex corner.
ACTION t9 End: two more kills at the throne. Louise, Vaida and Pent stay put on purpose, since the annex pair has nowhere better to go. Vaida's 18 HP is the likeliest loss this phase.

content.thinking: Vaida's death quote showed up on turn 9's enemy phase, so she has probably fallen. A single loss doesn't call for a restart, since the throne holds with two turns left, so I'm advancing the dialogue.

Turn 10 of 11: Hector is still at full health, 51/51. I'm holding position, having Hector strike the adjacent archer and Hawkeye attack with Steel, but checking Hawkeye's HP first since poison is wearing him down.

content.text: ACTION t10 Hector: Wolf Beil on the Poison-bow Morph, exactly 27 damage against 27 HP at 82 hit, no counter. A one-hit kill if it connects.
Dead. Now Hawkeye: stepping through his menu with a look at each screen.
The Steel-axe switch worked: only 1 use spent, and Tomahawk stayed at 6. Steel again.

content.thinking: Hawkeye is capped at Lv20 with only 12 axe uses left, and the Flux Morph deals just 1 damage, so I'm holding off on the attack and waiting instead. The harmless Flux will stay as a blocker on his east side, saving the Steel axe for later chapters.

content.text: Moving the highlight four down to Wait and confirming, then opening the Unit list for a full HP read.
Louise holds at 31/34 in the corner, and Vaida's tile south of her is now empty, confirming the death. Louise stays: the corner still limits her attackers. Ending the turn.
ACTION t10 End: Hector killed one and Hawkeye held on purpose to save uses. Pent and Louise stay idle. Next is the last counted turn.
Turn 10's enemy phase is nearly over. Hector is still at 50 of 51 while taking attacks on the throne, and Louise has enemies closing on her corner. One more player turn after this.
Last Turn, and Hector is at 52/52 after another level. Reading everyone's HP before the final phase.

content.thinking: Vaida has dropped off the roster, and the other six units are all healthy. Next I'm planning to survive one more enemy phase, with Hector taking the free XP on the adjacent archer using his Wolf Beil.

content.text: ACTION t11 Hector: Wolf Beil on the Poison-bow Morph, 28 against 29 HP at 84 hit. It won't quite die, but there's no counter, so the XP is free.
Hector's done. Opening the field menu from the empty tile three to the right.
ACTION t11 End: only Hector acted. Hawkeye, Pent and Louise hold on purpose, saving their uses. Nobody can reach the throne, so this should run out the clock.
Reinforcements have arrived: the Ostian army is on the map asking after Hector, so the chapter's been survived. Pressing through the ending one batch at a time, watching for prompts.
Athos is asking for the legendary items, which sets up the next chapter. Skipping the cutscene with Start, one press at a time.
ACTION t11 Side quest: Yes. The general strategy says to always accept side missions, and this should be Chapter 31x, "Battle Preparations".
ACTION t11 Save: pick the highlighted Ch. 31 slot, the one in use, per the runbook's save table.
Saved. This looks like the chapter-title crest coming in, so I'm waiting and screenshotting it for the record.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Promoting Units

Fire Emblem has a mechanic known as promotion, where a unit advances to a stronger class. A unit must be at least level 10 to be promoted, although it can go as high as level 20 before being promoted. It is up to you to decide when it is appropriate to promote a unit.

In virtually all cases, a unit is promoted by using a specific consumable item that matches its class. For example, a knight can use a knight crest to be promoted to a general.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

- If an objective is unclear, actually commit Wait on special tiles (gates especially): some triggers only fire on Wait, and the menu looks ordinary beforehand. Backing out proves nothing.
- Sprites stand taller than their tile, so check the unit panel before pressing `A`. `A` on an empty tile opens the field menu, and blind follow-up presses can land on Suspend. L also cycles to Merlinus, who can't act.
- Lyn and Eliwood are on the field as lords: either one dying is an instant GAME OVER. Read their HP at Preparations (only 23 and 21 in Ch. 26) and keep them out of first-turn reach. A lord carried by Hector cannot be targeted.
- In the forecast, the "x2" marker covers the last digit of Mt ("2x2" can mean 28, hit twice). After a Dance, send the cursor move in a separate press call, or it gets swallowed and the next A opens the field menu. Ninian's Dance also refreshes a ballista rider for a second shot.
- Press only one or two `A`s through mid-phase dialogue: spare `A`s carry into your player phase and open a unit's menu. The turn also ends by itself once every unit but Merlinus has acted, so check the screen before opening the field menu. Staff-capable units get Staff at the top of the menu, not Attack, and it shows only if a wounded ally is in range.
- Green NPCs you must protect can be Rescued if Aid is at least their Con, and a carried unit cannot be targeted. Check the menu next to them. In the Preparations item screens the hand sits left of its option, so read the highlight before A: Give all is right of Trnsfr and empties the unit into the convoy.
- Enemy-phase bait works: a sturdy unit on a Fort or forest counters while Pent and Louise kill from two tiles, where most melee enemies cannot counter. After a kill or level-up the camera shifts, so re-read the cursor before pressing A; blind presses reached End and Suspend in Ch. 29.
- Weapons break mid-chapter and the menu silently drops Attack, so blind `A`s fall into Item and onto Discard. Screenshot the unit menu first. A range 1-2 weapon spends uses on counters at both ranges; a melee axe saves them. Preparations Trade > List can pull items from undeployable units, and a lord may use a Heaven seal at Lv10+ there.

- Ninian and Nils left the map in a scripted event on t4 enemy phase; I did not see Ninian afterwards and did not check whether she is still on the Unit list.

content.text:
Chapter 31 is won on the first attempt: the throne held through all 11 turns, and the game is now on the Chapter 31x Preparations screen ("Get supplies"). I accepted the side quest and saved over the highlighted Ch. 31 slot. Start skipped the cutscene and any title card, so the Preparations header is the record of the new chapter. `run_state.json` and the strategy notes are updated.
